events.title: The Western Roman Empire Falls
events.description: The Germanic leader Odoacer captured Ravenna and deposed Romulus Augustus, the teenage emperor. Odoacer then proclaimed himself King of Italy.
events.significance: Historians often use this date to mark the end of the Western Roman Empire. It is a traditional dividing line between antiquity and the Middle Ages in Europe.

events.title: Los Angeles Is Founded
events.description: Forty-four Spanish settlers founded the pueblo of El Pueblo de Nuestra Señora la Reina de los Ángeles.
events.significance: The small farming settlement grew into Los Angeles, one of the largest and most influential cities in the world.

events.title: The French Third Republic Is Proclaimed
events.description: After Emperor Napoleon III was captured during the Franco-Prussian War, he was deposed in Paris. The Third Republic was declared.
events.significance: The Third Republic lasted until 1940. It was France's longest-lived government since the 1789 Revolution.

events.title: Edison Switches On the First Commercial Power Plant
events.description: Thomas Edison started the Pearl Street Station, which lit up about a square mile of Lower Manhattan.
events.significance: It was an early landmark in the commercial supply of electricity. It showed that central power stations could light whole neighborhoods.
